subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode options & migration next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@lumina.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment mode recap & next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from today
- Primary goals: reduce per-token cost, meet EU data residency/controls, and improve production latency (p95 target < 300ms).
- Current setup: you mentioned a mix of OtherLLM API + an internal GPU cluster for peak workloads.
- Key constraints: SOC2 is required for sensitive logs; timeline for pilot is ~6–8 weeks.

Recommended next-step plan (high level)
1) Pilot on Redwood Hosted API to validate prompt/QA and latency quickly (low-friction).
2) If you need predictable throughput and reserved capacity for production, evaluate Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools).
3) For strict data residency / on-prem requirements we can discuss Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem package).

To help us qualify the right path, could you confirm the following?
- Typical request size (avg tokens in/out) and peak concurrency (rps or concurrent requests)
- Any hard latency SLOs beyond the p95 target above
- Which datasets must remain in EU or be on-prem
- Expected monthly token volume and target budget range for production
- Who will own the procurement/PO (legal/procurement contact)

I’m looping Dylan (ops) on this thread to help with capacity and rough pricing numbers. After you send the answers above, recommend a 45-min tech deep-dive with Dev (our infra PM) to map migration details from OtherLLM and your GPU cluster.

Attachments: infra_diagram.pdf (what you shared in the call)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow if easier.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samir Shah <samir@lumina.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-16T08:21:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode recap & next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. A few answers + context from our side: 

Current infra details
- Prod traffic today: avg ~25 req/s, bursts to ~60 during batch processing windows; average payload ~150 tokens in / ~120 tokens out.
- Latency: we try to stay p95 < 300ms for UI flows; background jobs can be higher.
- We run a mix: currently routed through OtherLLM's hosted API for most calls; fallback to our k8s cluster (4x A100) for heavy loads and fine-tuned model runs.
- Data residency: must keep EU customer PII in EU region; some non-PII logs can live elsewhere.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II baseline required; we also have an internal security questionnaire.
- Timeline: pilot in 6–8 weeks, production rollout by Q4 if pilot looks good.

Procurement: legal/procurement contact is Claire Dupont (claire.dupont@lumina.ai) — she’ll own contract review.

Attachments: attaching our infra diagram (infra_diagram.pdf) and a short cost-expectation doc.

Two quick questions for Redwood: 
1) Do you have a migration guide for moving from OtherLLM hosted APIs and for offloading model serving from an on-prem GPU cluster?
2) Rough ballpark on Dedicated reserved capacity pricing (we’re trying to size ROI vs keeping our cluster).

If helpful I can share a short spreadsheet with month 1–3 expected volume. Would be useful before the deep-dive.

—Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform, Lumina Labs
samir@lumina.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@lumina.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-16T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode recap & next steps

Thanks Samir — great detail, this is exactly what we needed. 

Answers to your questions + next steps:
1) Migration guides: yes — we have playbooks for (a) switching API traffic from OtherLLM to Redwood (auth/token mapping, prompt parity checks, rate limits), and (b) migrating model workloads from self-hosted GPU clusters (KV cache export, model checkpoint compatibility, warmers). We’ll bring Dev on the deep-dive to go through those steps.

2) Ballpark pricing for Dedicated (very rough at this stage):
- Reserved pool equivalent to your peak: starts around $Xk/month for a 2–3 node reserved pool for steady 25rps workloads; can scale to handle bursts. We’ll provide a tailored estimate once we see the monthly token/throughput spreadsheet.

Recommended path based on constraints:
- Pilot: Redwood Hosted API in EU region to validate prompts and latency quickly (fastest path).
- Production: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) if you need predictable performance and cost controls.
- Regulated / on-prem: Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) if you need data isolated to your network or air-gapped.

I attached a short deployment-mode comparison and a draft mutual action plan to get alignment. Proposed next steps:
- You share the 1–3 month expected volume spreadsheet (Samir)
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive with Dev and Dylan to map migration/ops runbook (propose Wed 2026-06-23 or Thu 2026-06-24)
- We’ll follow with a tailored Dedicated pricing estimate and a draft MSA for legal to review

Attachments: redwood-deployment-comparison.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll wait for the spreadsheet and will block time for the deep-dive once you confirm availability.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Marissa — this looks good. Claire and I confirmed the timeline internally. We’ll: 

- Share the 1–3 month volume spreadsheet by EOD Monday (will include token estimates and expected growth).
- Claire will coordinate procurement and loop in legal for the MSA review.
- We prefer the Wed 23rd deep-dive at 10:00 CET if that works for your team. Please send a calendar invite.

Two outstanding asks before the deep-dive: 
1) Can you send SOC2 Type II evidence and pointer to your security questionnaire responses?
2) Any notes on how you handle model weights/finetune artifacts when customers move from self-hosted to your Dedicated environment (retention, encryption, transfer tooling)?

If you can include those in the drive link or attach ahead of Wed we’ll be in good shape.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Samir
